title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity this week, from NASA's expanded contracts to SpaceX's latest Starship launch. Meanwhile, military satellite networks are getting a hefty financial boost as the industry gears up for a more resilient future.

themes.title: NASA's Contract Expansion
themes.body: NASA is adding missions to its commercial crew contract with SpaceX, signaling a commitment to maintain a steady flow of astronauts to the ISS. This move also underscores the agency's reliance on private partners for operational capabilities.

themes.title: Military Satellite Investments
themes.body: The Space Force's $437 million award to Viasat and SES for a military satellite network highlights the increasing prioritization of satellite resilience. As geopolitical tensions rise, such investments are becoming essential for national security.

themes.title: Blue Origin's Investigation Closure
themes.body: Blue Origin has wrapped up its investigation into the New Glenn launch failure, which is a relief for a company that has faced its share of challenges. The resolution may pave the way for renewed confidence in their future launch capabilities.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Delays
themes.body: The ongoing delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests, now slipping for the third consecutive quarter, raise questions about the U.S. military's readiness in this critical area. As adversaries advance, the pressure is on to accelerate these developments.
